gaps.sentence: ___ students joined the trip this year than last.

gaps.explanation: 'Warm enough' means sufficiently warm; 'enough' follows the adjective.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the two proposals has been approved so far.
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of the two' — 'none' is for three or more.

gaps.sentence: I put ___ sugar in your tea by mistake.
gaps.explanation: 'Too much' is used before uncountable nouns like sugar; 'too sugar' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ patience with excuses; deliver on time or do not bother coming.
gaps.explanation: 'Has no patience with' — 'no' directly negates the noun.

gaps.sentence: Three of the six books were mine; ___ were my sister's.
gaps.hint: the defined remainder of a set of six
gaps.explanation: 'The others' refers to the specific remaining books in the known set of six.

gaps.sentence: He took ___ notice of the warning and carried on as before.
gaps.explanation: 'Take little notice of' means to pay hardly any attention; 'notice' is uncountable here.

gaps.hint: price per item comes at the end
gaps.explanation: 'Fifteen pounds each' means fifteen pounds per ticket; 'every' cannot stand alone in this position.
